items.title: The Fitting-type ideal attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules is well defined up to powers of the nonzerodivisor depending on the Euler characteristic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma fixes a nonzerodivisor f in a ring A and two bounded complexes M^bullet and N^bullet of finite free A-modules representing the same object of D(A), and asserts that f^m I_i(M^bullet, f) = f^n I_i(N^bullet, f) whenever the integers m, n satisfy a displayed Euler-characteristic condition (source lines 27892-27906). The proof localizes at every prime to reduce to comparing a complex with its sum with a trivial two-term complex (proof lines 27908-27917), and then splits into the three cases j not in {i-1, i, i+1}, j = i+1, j = i and j = i-1 (proof lines 27918-27998). The core is a minors computation: the generator sets of the two ideals are compared by exhibiting the relevant matrix in block form T with diagonal blocks T_1 and T_2 and invoking the formula for ideals generated by minors of a block matrix, which combined with I_0(T_2) = A, I_1(T_2) = A and I_p(T_2) = 0 for p >= 2 gives the required equality. This is the only candidate of the batch whose proof is a complete multi-case computation, and the author keeps the localization-and-induction reduction as an explicit step.
